t:
(a) In General.—There are authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2006 and each subsequent fiscal year such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act and the amendments made by this Act. 
    (b) Other Amounts.—Amounts appropriated pursuant to the authorization of appropriations in subsection (a) shall be in addition to the amounts otherwise available to carry out this Act and the amendments made by this Act. 
    (c) Availability.—Amounts appropriated pursuant to the authorization of appropriations under subsection (a) are authorized to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations, states that they are in addition to other available amounts, and makes them available until expended. There is no tempting participation reading: it contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only authorizes funding, says the funds add to other available amounts, and lets them remain available until spent. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The phrase 'to carry out this Act' does not bring in any participation steps from elsewhere in the Act, because this section itself has no outside-party involvement in a federal decision.
opus.s: There are authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2006 and each subsequent fiscal year such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act and the amendments made by this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** It might seem that funding "to carry out this Act" pulls in any participation steps found elsewhere in the Act. That doesn't work. The definition asks what this section itself does, and this section only authorizes and describes appropriations. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision here.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard authorization of appropriations clause. It deals solely with the availability of federal funds and does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government. There are no mentions of public hearings, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: There are authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2006 and each subsequent fiscal year such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act and the amendments made by this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "appropriations" imply a process involving outside entities (like contractors or grantees), but the text itself only authorizes the funding mechanism. It does not describe any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory role for non-federal parties. The actors involved are Congress (appropriating) and the federal agency (spending), both inside the government.
